text:
Aisha R: Hey folks, first-week setup snag. I switched my laptop to Colima and my postgres in docker-compose fails with: "FATAL: data directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data" has wrong ownership". I originally had the db data mounted to ~/code/app/pgdata. Also my app intermittently gets "ERR NOAUTH" from Redis even though I put REDIS_PASSWORD in .env. Any quick debugging tips?

Ben K: welcome Aisha! two common mac/Colima gotchas. For Postgres the host-bind ends up owned by root inside the Colima VM so postgres refuses to run. We usually avoid host mounts for PG in favor of named volumes. If you must bind-mount, fix ownership inside Colima.

Ben K: Steps I run:```bash
# enter VM and fix owner to postgres uid
colima ssh
sudo chown -R 999:999 /home/youruser/code/app/pgdata
exit
# restart DB
docker compose up -d db
```

Chris: Another quick check: if an earlier failed init created files as root, you might need to wipe the directory (`rm -rf`) and let Postgres re-init after ownership fix. Also ensure your compose uses the same PG image we recommend (check runbook) because alpine/slim images can miss extension packages.

Aisha R: After chown-ing inside colima PG started, thanks. But during init my seed SQL that creates pgvector errors with: "could not open extension control file \"pgvector.control\"". I'm using postgres:15-alpine in compose.

Ben K: yep alpine often lacks the Debian package. We build our dev image FROM postgres:15 and apt-install postgresql-15-pgvector. Easiest fix: switch to repo dev image or non-alpine base, or add installation to your Dockerfile.

Chris: short example Dockerfile:```Dockerfile
FROM postgres:15
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y postgresql-15-pgvector 
```

Aisha R: Redis: I ran `docker compose exec redis redis-cli -a "$REDIS_PASSWORD" ping` inside the container and it returns PONG. My app still hit ERR NOAUTH sometimes.

Ben K: Usually that means your app is talking to a different Redis instance or the env-file wasn't loaded. Check `docker ps` for stray redis containers and `docker inspect` the one you think is running. Also note `docker compose` (v2) and `docker-compose` (v1) behave slightly differently with env files and overrides.

Ben K: Commands:```bash
docker ps --filter ancestor=redis --format "{{.Names}}\t{{.Image}}\t{{.Status}}"
docker compose --env-file .env.dev up -d  # if you use .env.dev
docker compose exec redis env | grep REDIS
```

Aisha R: Found an old redis container leftover from earlier experiments. Stopped it and the app now authenticates fine. Also swapped to the repo dev image and the pgvector init succeeded.

infra-bot: Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/local-db-setup  See sections: "Colima ownership quirks", "PG image recommendations & extensions", "Redis env-file gotchas".

Chris: tiny tip: if you want host tools (pgAdmin/psql) to talk to the containerised DB without stopping local Postgres, map to a different host port like 55432:5432. Saves a lot of brew-service juggling.

Aisha R: Thanks y'all! Switching to named volumes + repo image fixed everything. Happy to paste my exact commands to the runbook if helpful. Appreciate the warm welcome :wave:
